Complete upstream catalog: morphology analysis

84,200 galaxies requested; 252,600 object–band rows retained. The object IDs exactly match the upstream catalog. There is no availability or morphology selection. The earlier 75-ID report was an initial pilot and is superseded for coverage by this run.

Measured findings

Band C median A raw median A corrected median A corrected valid A corrected negative (%) Gini aperture median M20 aperture median
g 2.478 0.6826 -0.0507 82177 70.83 0.4977 -1.506
r 2.571 0.6065 -0.0409 79828 68.36 0.518 -1.619
i 2.608 0.7154 -0.07489 80330 78.13 0.485 -1.564

The complete baseline images support corrected A for roughly 95–98% of requested objects per band, unlike the limited wide-image pilot. Nevertheless, most corrected A values are negative: the sky correction is large relative to the minimized galaxy residual. Together with the synthetic symmetric-galaxy stress test, this is a reason to investigate noise/interpolation bias before interpreting corrected A as intrinsic structure. Negative measurements have been retained; they are not zero-clipped.

Concentration differs across bands. Matched-object median C differences are −0.0968 for g−r, −0.1344 for g−i and −0.0425 for r−i; these descriptive differences do not isolate stellar-population effects from PSF, noise or aperture changes. Both raw S profiles have strong rank agreement (Spearman about 0.994–0.995), but removing the Conselice factor of ten still leaves median raw-profile offsets of approximately −0.054 to −0.072. Corrected-profile rank correlations are 0.966–0.978. Neither result selects a physically preferred profile.

Gini and M20 provide additional, non-identical information: their within-band rank correlations are approximately −0.64 to −0.78. These are aperture-based values, so published segmentation-based Gini–M20 classification boundaries are inapplicable. Signed M20 moments can also produce atypical values when noise contributes substantial negative flux. The positive-weight shape diagnostics are descriptive and have no PSF or low-signal bias correction here.

Dataset and configuration alignment

The recent upstream configuration sky_subtracted_2_onmr2__detr_and_vit_all_multiband_1024_wide_legacy_fliplr_object_centered__galfit_1024_sanitized__per_band_mag_reff__xy_2_5arcsec and the 256-pixel configuration sky_subtracted_2_onmr2__detr_and_vit_all_multiband_256__per_band_magnitude_optimization__r_constant_offset both select the same concatenated-detr-vit-all.fits catalog. This run uses its complete original ordering and r/g/i bands. It reads the existing sky-subtracted 256-pixel images and target-preserving masks shared by the upstream 256-pixel configurations. The wide-image experimental products have different coverage and preprocessing; those are not substituted for the baseline images. The symlink to the external data drive is resolved explicitly. GALFIT models and fitted radii are not inputs to these measurements.

Input availability: 252,504 image–mask pairs; 96 missing combinations before measurement. The statuses below also retain WCS, aperture, photometry and other failures.

C, raw/sky/corrected A, and both raw/sky/corrected S profiles are retained together. Gini, M20, axis ratio, ellipticity and position angle are additional aperture diagnostics. A null value is a failed or unavailable measurement, never an implicit zero.

Additional metric definitions

  • Gini_aperture_v1 measures absolute flux inequality inside the unmasked circular CAS aperture.
  • M20_aperture_v1 measures the signed second moment of the brightest 20% of signed total flux, relative to the signed total second moment at the flux centroid. Nonpositive moments are flagged.
  • The shape diagnostics use explicitly positive flux weights in that same aperture. Axis ratio is the square root of the covariance eigenvalue ratio; ellipticity is 1−q. The angle is in image coordinates, not celestial position angle, and is unstable for round sources.

These aperture adaptations are not statmorph's segmentation-based Gini/M20. They have no validated classification thresholds here. The formula background is documented in Lotz et al. (2004) and the statmorph reference source. Exact formulas and limitations are in the repository's docs/EXTENDED_METHODS.md.

Interpretation and remaining work

No user decision prevented this processing. Reference matching, realistic noise/PSF injection recovery and segmentation sensitivity remain scientific validation tasks, not permission gates. The 144-case pilot stress test showed raw-A noise sensitivity and negative corrected-A bias; it is not a DES uncertainty calibration. The corner-only sky method remains unchanged under shared method v3, (v3 adds a flagged fallback for the SciPy empty-direction optimizer error), so the larger run is directly traceable without silently replacing its scientific definition. Both S profiles remain v1.

Signed sky-subtracted values and valid negative corrections are retained. Gini is computed from absolute pixel values; the shape diagnostics' positive weights can bias noisy images. No morphology classes, merger labels, preferred S profile or population-causal conclusions are assigned from these uncalibrated values.

Extended diagnostic flags: {"m20_nonpositive_moment": 524, "m20_nonpositive_flux": 134}.

Exploratory comparison, not a benchmark or proof of physical accuracy. Both clumpiness profiles differ in smoothing, central exclusion and ×10 scaling: their numerical values are not directly interchangeable. Corrected A/S require a clean sky tile; a missing correction is shown as missing, not as raw or zero. The surviving valid subset can be biased.
